business_problem: UNICEF wanted to help young people in Brazil find practical green-skills pathways and climate-action opportunities instead of leaving their sustainability interest disconnected from education and work options.
solution_summary: Capgemini used the 2025 Global Data Science Challenge to deliver UNICEF a working agentic-AI blueprint for guiding young people in Brazil toward green learning and career opportunities. Teams built on curated green-job and training datasets using AWS infrastructure—Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, the Strands Agents SDK, and Amazon SageMaker AI—together with Mistral AI language models. The winning Green Career Assistant combines four layers: data wrangling to clean and map skills/jobs/training data, agentic dialogue to interpret a user's context, a knowledge graph that links roles to learning pathways in a verifiable way, and a human-in-the-loop review step for transparency and fairness. The result is an explainable recommendation assistant with token and carbon monitoring that UNICEF can implement and extend, starting with Brazil, instead of a static catalog of opportunities.

data_flow: Curated green-job and training datasets are cleaned and linked into a knowledge graph, then the assistant uses agentic dialogue to interpret a user's goals and recommend relevant opportunities. AWS services and Mistral models power the reasoning layer, while human review and token/carbon monitoring keep the recommendations transparent and operationally responsible.
